summary: Powell County, MT camp with an elevated firefinder platform, built 1938 and abandoned 1960; the Association lists it as an abandoned platform, and no source describes it today.

facts.status_note: The Fire Lookout Association lists it as an abandoned platform; no source says whether any of it remains

access.note: No access source found for the site

events.note: Camp with elevated firefinder platform, per firelookout.com

evidence.supports: about 18 miles northeast of Seeley Lake
built 1938 as a camp with elevated firefinder platform
names the Lolo and Flathead national forests together
coordinates 47.30739 north, 113.14111 west; type platform; status abandoned

corrections.why: The Association's list says Platform Abandoned, which does not say the platform is gone; no source says what remains

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rex's page names the Lolo National Forest; firelookout.com names the Lolo and Flathead National Forests together. The record uses Lolo; the story notes both.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the build and abandonment dates and the elevation come from one firelookout.com page; the Association list and Rex's page add the status and land location. Nothing on staffing, fires or the site today was found in the search. A Watch Duty listing (search snippet only, page not opened) shows a 3-acre 'Foolhen Fire' on Foolhen Mountain dated 27 Sep 2025; no source ties it to the platform, so it is left out of the story.
